solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Right to assess wood cut for BBQ, perhaps

indicators.note: the right-hand end of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of assess
teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: Someone claims the right to judge which timber to chop for the barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right to assess' reads like an entitlement, but it only means the right-hand letter of assess.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak is a thick slice of meat, the classic thing grilled at a barbecue; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: School teaching year shows difference in pitch

parts.note: SCH is an abbreviation for school
an ism is a doctrine or teaching
A stands for annus, Latin for year

explanation.surface: A school's year of teaching reveals how far apart two notes are.
explanation.definitionFit: A schisma is a tiny musical interval, the minute gap in pitch between two nearly identical notes in tuning theory.

clue.text: She crosses a line in Parisienne's very old hat, right?

parts.note: très is French for very, as a Parisian woman would say it
passé means out of date
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman in a very dated hat seems to be overstepping the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser goes where they have no right to be, crossing a boundary line onto someone else's property.

clue.text: Fairness would be sovereignty without right

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: regality is royal power or sovereignty
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A political thought: fairness is just royal power with justice removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Egality is an old word for equality, treating everyone the same, which is fairness.

clue.text: Soak vessel upside-down in large bowl

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upside-down flips the letters to run from bottom to top

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it
Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat is soaked upside down in a big basin.
explanation.definitionFit: A krater is an ancient Greek wide-mouthed bowl for mixing wine with water.

clue.text: Liberal point on according rave review

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the Liberal-and-point chunk follows the other piece

parts.note: ACC is an abbreviation for according
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
your aim is your point or purpose

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician picks out a point in a glowing write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the Liberal-plus-point chunk after the abbreviation for according.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public praise, which is what a rave review delivers.

clue.text: Wholly excessive people will dig in here?

definitions.note: a clause: the place where people will dig; 'people' also does duty in the wordplay

parts.note: all means wholly, completely
OTT stands for over the top
men are people

explanation.surface: A grumble that overzealous people will dig themselves in here.
explanation.walkthrough: The people go inside the abbreviation for over the top; there is no separate container word, so the clue relies on 'dig in' doing double work. An allotment is a rented garden plot, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a small plot of land rented for growing vegetables, where gardeners come to dig.

clue.text: Worked on a boat unprepared to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means the word is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: crude means raw, unprepared

explanation.surface: Someone served as a sailor without getting ready, by all accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To crew is to work as one of the people sailing a vessel, so crewed is past tense for working on a boat.

clue.text: These beaches could be packed solid

indicators.note: packing things moves them about, so the letters of the next word can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: These beaches might be crammed with people from end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public bathing beach or open-air pool, so lidos are such beaches.

clue.text: Fusses about spinning fail for Sturgeon

parts.note: A is short for about, as in approximate figures

indicators.note: spinning turns something round, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: fail is a Scots word for turf or sod, and Nicola Sturgeon is a Scottish politician

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a failure that leaves Nicola Sturgeon in a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Sturgeon, the former Scottish First Minister, signals a Scots word: fail there means a piece of turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Ados are fusses or commotions, as in 'much ado about nothing'.

clue.text: Gosh! Chinese people turned up mimic

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Han are China's majority ethnic group

explanation.surface: Surprise as some Chinese people appear doing impressions.
explanation.definitionFit: The mynah is a bird famous for copying human speech, so it is a natural mimic.

clue.text: Dependable sort returning dress, fairly upset about daughter (10, two words)

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to rig out is to dress

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap round the next piece
upset things are knocked out of their order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A reliable person brings back a dress, rather annoyed about their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl Friday is a loyal female assistant, named after Robinson Crusoe's faithful servant Man Friday, hence a dependable helper.

clue.text: Try hard to plough in historic fashion

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
ear is an archaic verb meaning to plough

explanation.surface: Instructions to make a real effort at ploughing the old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try hard' looks like one phrase, but Try is the definition and hard starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears a case in court, which is the legal sense of trying it.

clue.text: "Relax" — song to dominate utterly

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
slang: to own an opponent is to beat them completely

explanation.surface: 'Relax' is a song that topped the charts and swept all before it.
explanation.walkthrough: Relax was a famous Frankie Goes to Hollywood hit, which makes the quoted word look like a title rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to stretch out and rest, a plain synonym for unwinding.

clue.text: Lollard with fabulous felicity gaining frequency

indicators.note: gaining means taking on an extra piece, so one more letter joins the mix

parts.note: W is short for with

indicators.note: fabulous suggests something invented or fanciful, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
F is the symbol for frequency

explanation.surface: A medieval dissenter becomes increasingly blissful in a fairytale way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe, the 14th-century reformer, so a Lollard is a Wycliffite.

clue.text: Holm is historically obstructed

parts.note: taken as written
let once meant hindered, a sense kept in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A statement that some place called Holm was blocked off in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Holm looks like a place name, but it is a word for a small island, especially one in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A holm is a small island in a river or near a coast, the same thing as an islet.

clue.text: Near indifference over anonymous fashion in poet's sobriquet

indicators.note: near means almost, so the word stops one letter short
in a down clue, over means placed above, so the first piece goes on top of the rest

parts.note: apathy is lack of interest
A is short for anonymous
ton means the fashion, high style

explanation.surface: A poet's nickname nearly signals indifference to anonymous trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in poet's' marks a word found only in a poet's work; apathaton is Spenser's form of epithet.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathaton is Spenser's version of epithet, a descriptive name or nickname, which is what a sobriquet is.

clue.text: Tuning peg inserted in fixed musical instrument

indicators.note: something inserted in another thing sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: set means fixed or settled
the pins of a stringed keyboard are the pegs turned to tune it

explanation.surface: A tuning peg gets fitted into a stringed instrument that cannot be moved.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord-like keyboard instrument, so it is one musical instrument.

clue.text: Exodus finally seen in choice festival of liberation

indicators.note: a thing seen in another sits within it, so the letter is placed inside the word

parts.note: a peach is something excellent, a choice specimen

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of Exodus

explanation.surface: The close of the Exodus story features in a chosen celebration of freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links Exodus to the festival, which is apt since Passover remembers the Exodus, but the word only gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesach is the Hebrew name for Passover, which celebrates the Israelites' liberation from slavery in Egypt.

clue.text: Protected animal is disturbed in a brook beside duck

indicators.note: beside means next to, so the last piece is simply set alongside the rest
in places the word before it within the phrase that follows

parts.note: A plus RILL, a small stream
disturbed in the sense of mentally unbalanced
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: An animal is upset in a stream next to a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protected' sounds like conservation status; the armadillo is literally protected by its bony plates.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is a mammal covered in an armour of bony plates, so it is a protected animal in a literal sense.

clue.text: Paper which is not read can curl (7, two words)

parts.note: can is slang for toilet
to curl is to roll up

explanation.surface: An unread newspaper might be rolled up into a cylinder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' suggests a newspaper, but this one is toilet paper. Loo is everyday British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A loo roll is a roll of toilet paper, paper that is used rather than read.

clue.text: Fellow in shifting focus on mobile refuse

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the material above it
in puts the first piece inside the jumbled letters
shifting letters move about, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
F is short for fellow
M is short for mobile

explanation.surface: A man shifts his attention to his mobile phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Offscum is an old word for scum or dregs, worthless matter thrown away as rubbish.

clue.text: Fancy term for paratactically set and in continuance

definitions.text: Fancy term for paratactically set and in continuance

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or embellish, so the collected letters are rearranged
a term is an end point, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of paratactically
taken as written
taken as written
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: A grammarian's gloss: a posh word for clauses placed side by side and carrying on.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue defines the answer; read in parts, it supplies every letter. The joke is that it uses 'and', the very word an asyndeton leaves out.
explanation.definitionFit: Asyndeton is the rhetorical omission of conjunctions, setting clauses side by side (paratactically) as in 'I came, I saw, I conquered'.

clue.text: Ultimate in rearing previously earnest foster-kids from Fife

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the turned word
in a down clue, rearing means rising up, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: sad once meant serious or earnest, an archaic sense
ULT is the abbreviation for ultimate

explanation.surface: The last thing in bringing up foster children in Fife used to be seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' looks like part of the foster-children picture, but it turns the old word for earnest upside down. Fife is a Scottish region, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dault is a Scots word for a foster child, so daults are foster children in Scotland.

clue.text: Bleeding "Circle of Life"

parts.note: a circle is shaped like O
o' is a shortened form of of
zing means vitality, liveliness

explanation.surface: An irritable aside about the song title 'Circle of Life', from The Lion King.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like the song title; the words are three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Oozing means seeping out slowly, as blood does from a wound, so it fits bleeding.

clue.text: What stands in front of hearth in a study?

definitions.text: What stands in front of hearth in a study?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places that single letter inside the word for study

parts.note: to scan is to study closely

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of hearth

explanation.surface: A riddle: what is the thing standing by the fireplace in the den?
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a bin for ashes set before a fireplace, perhaps in a study.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashcan is a container for ashes or rubbish, the kind of bin that might stand in front of a fireplace.

clue.text: We resist Article 50 being overlooked from upcoming opening

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, upcoming means rising, so the word reads from bottom to top
something overlooked is left out, so that numeral's letter is dropped

parts.note: a slit is a narrow opening
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Opponents of Brexit declare they will resist being ignored over Article 50.
explanation.walkthrough: Article 50 is the EU treaty clause used for Brexit, but here Article and 50 are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Antis are opponents, people against something, so they could say 'we resist'.

clue.text: European run out aboard Geordie coaler

indicators.note: aboard means on the ship, so the letters are put inside the vessel

parts.note: a cat was a coal-carrying ship of north-east England, where Geordies live
RO is the cricket abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A European is dismissed in cricket while on board a Tyneside coal ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne; the cat was a broad collier ship from that coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croat is a person from Croatia, a European country, so a Croat is one example of a European.

clue.text: Flipping arrogant gasp with respect to following departure

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: poh is an exclamation of contempt
of can mean concerning, with respect to
F is short for following

explanation.surface: An exasperated aside about someone's haughty intake of breath as the next person leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive, but it reverses the contemptuous exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hop-off is a start or setting off, as in hop off for leaving, so it names a departure.

clue.text: Shocking manager losing the second half

indicators.note: losing the second half means dropping the back part of the word, keeping only its start

parts.note: a director is a manager of a company

explanation.surface: A boss is dreadful after the team loses the second half of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful or terrible, which is a sense of shocking.

clue.text: Zulu guzzles out of tin holders

parts.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: out of means without, so the metal's symbol is removed from the word

parts.note: to snarf is to eat greedily
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A Zulu gulps food straight from the can.
explanation.definitionFit: A zarf is a metal holder for a handleless coffee cup, used in the Middle East, so zarfs are holders.

clue.text: Eliot bemused by translator's poem

indicators.note: by means next to, so the jumbled name sits after the abbreviation

parts.note: TR is an abbreviation for translator

indicators.note: bemused means confused, so the poet's name is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: T. S. Eliot is puzzled by a translator's version of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A triolet is a short French verse form of eight lines with two rhymes and repeated lines, so it is a kind of poem.

clue.text: Cross with one starting to complain about animals

parts.note: a zo is a cross between a yak and a cow
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: starting points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of complain

explanation.surface: Someone angry that a person is beginning to grumble about the animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry', but it is a noun: a zo (also dzo) is a Himalayan yak-cow hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoic means relating to animals or animal life, so it describes things about animals.

clue.text: I ran with tailor fittingly making what looks long short

indicators.note: a tailor fits cloth by cutting and reshaping it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ran to a tailor to have a garment that looks long shortened to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: In prosody an irrational syllable is a long one made to count as short, which the definition describes.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical metre, an irrational syllable has a length that does not match its metrical slot, typically a long syllable standing where a short one belongs.

clue.text: Paradigm of western dress? Don't change it, sunshine

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning leave as written
sunshine and son are both casual British forms of address to a man

explanation.surface: A model outfit for the Wild West, and a warning to someone not to alter it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western' means the cowboy film genre, not the West in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stetson is the broad-brimmed cowboy hat, the emblematic item of clothing in a Western film.

clue.text: Sound argument from which ma'll break free mug

parts.note: go means in perfect working order, as in 'all systems go'

indicators.note: from which marks the word that something will be taken away from

parts.note: a lemma is a proposition used in an argument or proof
ma will break away, leaving the rest of the word

explanation.surface: A solid case, after which Mother will escape a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' could suggest a homophone, but here it means in good working order. A golem is also slang for a dolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the clay figure of Jewish legend, golem is slang for a stupid person, a sense close to mug, a dupe.
